newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Early Taiwan dollar edges lower on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Early Taiwan dollar edges lower on short-covering.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar edged lower in early Monday trade due to short-covering on the U.S. dollar, but dealers said persistently rising short-term interest rates would stabilise the rate.
After 45 minutes, at 0145 GMT, the local unit was at T$27.823 against Saturday's T$27.814 close.
Turnover through dealers was a light US$33 million.
"After days of Taiwan dollar appreciation, many banks are short of the U.S. dollar," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
The Taiwan dollar had risen for eight straight sessions in part because of persistently tight liquidity.
Dealers said current liquidity squeeze would keep the local unit at around current levels.
They said Hong Kong's looming midnight return to Chinese rule was having little impact on the currency market.
"I don't see Hong Kong's handover play an important role in today's foreign exchange market. The Taiwan dollar is already very stable. And that's precisely what the central bank wants," she said.
A range of T$27.80-83 was seen for Monday.
